items.response:
I'll write the local setup section of docs/onboarding.md: copy .env.example to .env.local, then pull the secrets from the 1Password vault acme-dev. I'll also note that billing changes need your review before anything lands, and I'll hold myself to that too. I don't have the install or start commands in front of me, so I'll check the repo's package.json and README for those rather than guess.
Action: Read package.json and the README, then draft the setup section in docs/onboarding.md for your review.

Sure. I haven't seen how the CLI is structured yet, so I'll look at the existing `invoices list` command and any other commands that already have a --json flag before writing anything. I'll make the JSON output plain, with no colors or table, so it pipes cleanly into jq, and add a test.
Action: Open the invoices list command in packages/cli, check how other commands handle --json, then implement the flag and run the CLI tests.

Here's what I did today from this conversation: I added a `maskIban` util in apps/web/lib/format.ts that strips spaces, uppercases, masks everything except the last 4 characters and regroups in 4s, with three tests in apps/web/lib/format.test.ts that pass. I also kicked off root lint and the full web suite in the background, and I haven't seen those results yet. I only have this conversation to go on, so I can't speak to anything earlier in the day.
Action: Check the lint and web suite results and then give you a final standup-ready summary.

I don't have anything in front of me about how the API is exposed publicly (ingress, load balancer, or certificate setup), and I don't want you repeating a guess to Priya. The best way to be informed is for me to look at the infra config for the API's ingress and where its TLS cert comes from.
Action: Search the infra directory (helm values, ingress and cert manifests) and give you a short summary of the public path and how cert renewal works.

I'll write a Playwright test that covers the full flow: new invoice, pick client, add a line, save, send. Per the repo's e2e setup it needs the dev server on port 3000 (`pnpm --filter web dev`) and runs via `pnpm --filter web e2e`. I'll use the 'New invoice' button label, use retrying assertions like expect(locator).toHaveText instead of reading rows once right after a click, and avoid the known pdf download failure in detail.spec.ts since it's a seed fixture gap.
Action: Look at the existing specs under apps/web/e2e/invoices for selectors and seed data, write the new spec, then start the dev server and run it.

Charts live in infra/helm with one chart per service, so I'll look at the api chart (values.yaml and values-prod.yaml and its templates) for the ExternalSecret and check whether POSTHOG_API_KEY is listed in its data or dataFrom mapping. Also worth confirming the key exists in AWS Secrets Manager under the path the ExternalSecret references. Note that infra/ is Priya's team's area, so any change there should go through her review.
Action: Read the api chart's ExternalSecret template and prod values and report whether POSTHOG_API_KEY is mapped.

Understood: the rule going forward is that every worker job handler is idempotent, keyed on the job id. I'll apply that to the webhooks handler first, so a redelivery after a pod restart is detected via the job id and skipped, and I'll keep comments to the why only. Before pushing I'll run the full suite with `pnpm test` rather than just the changed tests, per your rule. Also, the worker is on BullMQ/Redis now, so I'll build on that rather than anything RabbitMQ-related.
Action: Read services/worker/src/jobs/webhooks.ts, add the job-id idempotency check with a test, then run the full test suite.

I'll add a proper error boundary for the App Router in apps/web: an error.tsx for the dashboard route group with a 'Try again' button that calls reset(), plus a check that global-error.tsx covers the root layout case. The existing global-error.tsx already reports to Sentry with the digest and shows it as 'Error id', so I'll keep that behavior and reuse it. I'll commit on branch acme-447 with an imperative subject and a short body explaining why.
Action: Check out acme-447, look at the current error handling under app/(dashboard), write the fallback with a test, and commit.

I'll start by looking at Lena's PR to see exactly what it adds to apps/api and whether those config files were removed on main, so we can confirm and flag it on the PR. For CORS I'll change the api so it only allows origins listed in the comma-separated CORS_ORIGINS env var and nothing else, so unknown origins get no allow-origin header and an unset var allows none. I'll update the existing CORS tests to match.
Action: Inspect the PR diff and git history for the eslint/prettier files, then look at the api's current CORS setup and make the change.

On it: I'll fix all 5 on the zod branch (deps/zod-3.24.1): the optional discount guard in invoices.ts, the vatId narrowing in clients.ts, the two webhook.ts typing fixes and the ClientForm.tsx error in web. I'll commit work as I go rather than stashing anything, and re-run the repo-wide typecheck afterward to confirm it's clean.
Action: Check out deps/zod-3.24.1, apply the five fixes, and run `pnpm -r exec tsc --noEmit` plus the tests.

I'll add tsx as a devDependency in packages/cli. Because CI installs with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, I'll make sure pnpm-lock.yaml is updated and committed with it, otherwise the install job fails with ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE. I'll also check how scripts/ files are currently invoked so I can add a matching script entry if useful.
Action: Run `pnpm --filter <cli package> add -D tsx` in packages/cli, confirm the lockfile changed, and verify that a script in scripts/ runs with tsx.

Yes, tabular figures matter there. I'll apply a monospace font to the invoice number and amount columns, using JetBrains Mono with a generic monospace fallback. I'd also check whether the font is already loaded in the app, since I don't want to add a new font dependency blindly. Using `tabular-nums` is an alternative that keeps the current typeface, so I'll mention it.
Action: Find the invoices table column definitions in apps/web, check what fonts the app already loads, and add the monospace class to those two columns.

I'll add a `formatBytes` util in apps/web/lib that turns a byte count into a string like 1.2 MB, as a named export with no default export. The test will be a vitest file next to it with plain assertions (no jest-dom), covering 0 bytes, under 1 KB, exact unit boundaries and a fractional value like 1.2 MB. I need to decide on 1000 vs 1024 units, so I'll check how the attachments list or other code in the repo treats sizes and match that.
Action: Look for existing size formatting in apps/web, write lib/format-bytes.ts and its test, and run the web tests.

Going ahead with the invoice number collision fix: a per-org counter row incremented atomically with `UPDATE invoice_counters SET next = next + 1 WHERE org_id = $1 RETURNING next - 1`, in a new migration `0034_invoice_counters.sql` that backfills from current max numbers, and I'll update invoice-number.ts to use it. I'll keep the notes short, and the bucket stays parked with Priya.
Action: Write the migration and the invoice-number.ts change, add a parallel-creation test, and run the api tests.

Your 'ok' doesn't answer my question about which HTTP framework and version the API is on, and I don't want to write the guard in the wrong style. I'll check the api's package.json and its entry file myself instead of waiting. Then I'll write the x-org-id guard in the style that fits, returning a 403 problem+json when the header is missing or doesn't match a session org, and register it on the clients, invoices, orgs and uploads prefixes but not health or webhooks.
Action: Read apps/api/package.json and the app bootstrap to identify the framework and version, then implement the guard with tests.

Sure. I'll put the invoice number and amount columns in a monospace font, JetBrains Mono with a monospace fallback. The app uses Tailwind CSS v4 with CSS-first config in apps/web/app/globals.css, so I'll define the font as a token there via @theme and not create a tailwind.config.js. Then I'll apply it to those two columns.
Action: Add the font token to globals.css, apply the class to the invoice number and amount cells in the invoices table, and run the web tests.

I'll color the status column in `invoices list` with picocolors (paid green, overdue red, and sensible colors for the remaining statuses) and keep the --json path free of any color codes. Since this is a user-facing CLI change, I'll add a changeset with `pnpm changeset` before the PR. I'll also check how the existing snapshot tests handle ANSI output.
Action: Look at the invoices list command and its table rendering, add the picocolors status mapping, update the snapshot tests, and add the changeset.

I'd start with replicas: the worker already autoscales with KEDA on queue length (1 to 20 replicas, one per 50 messages), so a big backlog should already be pulling replicas up. First I'd check whether it is actually scaling or is capped at the max. Raising per-process concurrency from 5 is only safe if the reminder jobs are I/O bound and the downstream email provider and Postgres can take it. I don't have the current replica count or provider limits, so I'd look rather than guess.
Action: Check the KEDA ScaledObject in infra/k8s and the current replica count, then recommend a concrete change.

That's a CSV quoting problem: fields containing a comma, quote or newline need to be wrapped in double quotes with embedded quotes doubled, per RFC 4180. I'll find the clients export code, fix the escaping there, and add a test using the company name 'Smith, Jones & Co' plus one with an embedded double quote.
Action: Locate the clients CSV export, implement the escaping, add tests, and run them.

I'll add tsx as a devDependency in packages/cli with pnpm and look at how the scripts in scripts/ are run today so I can wire up a way to run them directly. I'll also check that the lockfile gets updated and committed with the change, since CI is likely to install from it.
Action: Run the pnpm add -D tsx command for packages/cli, verify the lockfile diff, and test running one of the scripts with tsx.

I'll rename getSessionClaims to readSessionClaims across the repo, including the definition, the callers, tests and any docs. I'll grep for every reference first so nothing is missed, then run the api tests and a typecheck to confirm. Since this is a pure rename unrelated to the clock skew fix, it's a small separate concern.
Action: Grep for all getSessionClaims references, rename them, and run the typecheck and api tests.

I don't have anything about how the API is exposed publicly or how its certificate renews, and I don't want to hand you a guess to repeat to Priya. I can find out from the repo's infra config: ingress, DNS, and whatever issues the certs.
Action: Search the infra directory for the api ingress/load balancer and certificate setup, then give you a short plain-language summary and a question or two to ask Priya.

I'll commit the five fixes to the zod branch (deps/zod-3.24.1) first, with a Conventional Commits message such as fix: narrow zod types after the 3.24.1 bump, and a short body saying why. Then for the CLI, `acme invoices list` already supports --json, so there may be nothing to add; I'd rather check the command in packages/cli than add a duplicate flag. If you meant different output, tell me what's missing.
Action: Commit to deps/zod-3.24.1, then inspect packages/cli/src/commands for invoices list and confirm what --json outputs.

I'll refactor the Stripe handler's event-type switch into a map of handlers keyed by event type, keeping behavior identical, with an unknown-event fallback. This is billing code, so I won't commit it. I'll leave the change uncommitted for your review, and note that the raw-body change from earlier is also still waiting on you.
Action: Read the stripe webhook handler, make the refactor, run the api tests including the stripe tests, and leave it uncommitted for you to review.

I'll write the local setup section of docs/onboarding.md. It will cover `pnpm dev` at the repo root to start web, api and worker together, copying .env.example to .env.local and pulling secrets from the 1Password vault acme-dev, and Docker needing to be running for the API tests since Testcontainers hangs if it's stopped. I'll also add the Apple Silicon note about not running under Rosetta and running `pnpm rebuild sharp` after switching Node versions, and mention Node 18 LTS. And noted on billing: I won't change billing code without your review, and the doc will say the same for the contractor.
Action: Draft the setup section in docs/onboarding.md and show it to you.

Two separate causes. The prod build error means a development Clerk publishable key (pk_test_) is being used in a production build, so the release branch build needs the live publishable key in the Vercel production env. The hydration warning on the due date column comes from the server rendering in UTC and the browser in local time, so I'll format that date with next-intl's useFormatter().dateTime(...) rather than toLocaleDateString or suppressHydrationWarning. I can't see the Vercel env settings from here, so I'd confirm which key the build is picking up. If the fix lives in .github/ workflows, that needs the platform team's approval.
Action: Check where the due date is formatted in the invoices page and fix it with useFormatter, then look at how the publishable key is configured for the release build and report back.

I'll add a ServiceMonitor to the worker helm chart (infra/helm/worker) that scrapes port 9464 at /metrics. I'll check how the chart names its service ports and whether the metrics port is exposed on the Service, since a ServiceMonitor selects on the Service. I also need to check what label Grafana's Prometheus uses to discover monitors, so I'll look at other ServiceMonitors in the repo rather than guess. Since infra/ is Priya's area, it should get her review.
Action: Inspect the worker chart's templates and values, add templates/servicemonitor.yaml with a values toggle, and render it with helm template to verify.

Noted on ESM: every package is type module, so I'll use import/export only, no require(). For the api logger I'll add redaction so bearer tokens, Authorization and cookie headers, and other secret-like fields are censored in logs, and I'll make sure error messages and serialized errors go through the same redaction. I'll add tests that a token in a request header and in an error message come out redacted.
Action: Look at how the api logger is set up, add the redaction config, and test it against an Authorization header and an error containing a bearer token.

I'll turn the event-type switch in the stripe handler into a map of handlers keyed by event type, keeping behavior the same and keeping a fallback for unhandled events. Since this is billing code, I'll leave it uncommitted for your review, as with the raw-body change. I'll run the stripe tests and the api suite to confirm nothing changed.
Action: Read the handler, refactor it into a handler map, run the tests, and leave the diff for you to review.

I'll fix the double delivery in services/worker/src/jobs/webhooks.ts by making the handler idempotent with the job id as the idempotency key, so a job re-run after a pod restart doesn't send the webhook twice. I'll treat that as the rule for every worker handler from here on, and I'll keep any comments to the why. I need to check how deliveries are recorded today to pick where the key is stored, so I'll look before choosing.
Action: Read the webhooks job and the worker queue setup, implement the idempotency check with a test that runs the same job id twice, and run the tests.

I'll add a proper error fallback for the dashboard: an error boundary page with a clear message and a 'Try again' button that calls reset(). I'd also check whether the app has a global-error setup, since a render crash in the root layout needs a different file than a route error. I'll check what Next.js version and router the app uses before choosing files. Then I'll commit on branch acme-447.
Action: Inspect apps/web's app directory and existing error handling, add the fallback with a test, and commit it on acme-447.

Setting the pool max to 10 connections per pod in apps/api/src/db/client.ts, matching what you and Priya agreed on. Pooler setup can matter here too, so I'll check how the client is configured and not touch other options. I'll note in the PR that pool size times max pods has to stay under the pooler's connection limit, and run the api tests.
Action: Open apps/api/src/db/client.ts, set max: 10, and run the api test suite.

I'll add a ServiceMonitor to the worker helm chart so Prometheus scrapes port 9464 at /metrics. Charts are in infra/helm with one per service, so I'll put it in the worker chart and gate it with a value, and check that the worker Service exposes that port. I'll follow whatever labels other ServiceMonitors in the repo use, if any, so Grafana's Prometheus picks it up, and render the chart with helm template to validate it.
Action: Inspect the worker chart templates and values, add the ServiceMonitor template, and verify with helm template.

The API's Postgres pool max is 10 connections per pod (set in apps/api/src/db/client.ts, the number you and Priya agreed on). Since the pool is capped at 10 and pods scale via HPA (3 to 12), the total can still hit the database limit, so the fix is to check total connections against the PgBouncer limit and not raise the pool. I don't know the current limit, so I'd check it.
Action: Look at the PgBouncer and Postgres max connection settings in the infra config and compare against 10 times the maximum api pods.

I'll fix all 5 typecheck errors on the zod bump branch: the optional discount guard in invoices.ts, the vatId narrowing in clients.ts, the two typing fixes in webhook.ts, and the ClientForm.tsx error in web. I'll run the repo-wide typecheck afterward and the tests to confirm it's clean. I won't commit unless you say so.
Action: Check out the zod branch (deps/zod-3.24.1), apply the five fixes, and run `pnpm -r exec tsc --noEmit` and the tests.

I'll add the copy share link button on the invoice preview, with the signing in apps/web/lib/share-link.ts: an HMAC over the invoice id plus an expiry, and the signature and expiry carried in the link. The signing secret must not reach the browser, so it can't be a NEXT_PUBLIC_ var; signing has to run on the server, and I'll expose it through a server action or route. I'll add a placeholder entry in .env.example with a note that the real value comes from the 1Password vault acme-dev, and keep the component small with a colocated test. I'll re-check for bugs and security issues, such as constant-time comparison and expiry checks, before calling it done.
Action: Look at the preview component and existing server action patterns, then write share-link.ts with tests and wire up the button.

I'll take both. For rate limiting I'll write a Fastify plugin using @fastify/rate-limit, 100 requests per minute per IP, backed by Redis. For the export bucket from yesterday, I don't have details of that conversation, so I'll search the infra directory for where it belongs and add it there. Then I'll use the gh CLI to open an issue tracking the bucket rollout. I'll check the api's plugin layout and existing Redis setup first.
Action: Look at how the api registers plugins and its Redis client, write the rate-limit plugin with a test, then search infra for the bucket location.

I'll add an invoice-reminders queue to the worker: a repeatable job that runs once a day per org, finds invoices due in 3 days, and enqueues a reminder email job for each. I need to look at how the existing queues are defined and how the email job takes its payload, and how the schedule is set up. I'll also check the timezone handling for 'due in 3 days' before choosing the boundaries.
Action: Read the worker's queue definitions and the email job, then implement the new queue with a test and run the worker tests.

Yes, I'll leave Marco a review comment on acme-215-clerk-verify saying that the diff dropped the isActiveMember check, so a still-valid token keeps working after someone leaves an org, and suggest restoring it as a DB lookup. For the /reports page, I don't know the app's layout yet, so I'd check the apps/web app directory for route groups and where other signed-in pages live, rather than guess a path.
Action: Post the review comment for Marco, then inspect apps/web/app and report where /reports should go.

Noted: never deploy to production on Fridays, and I'll treat that as a standing rule. Today is Thursday, so a tag is fine. I'll prepare the changelog for the tag from the commits and changesets since the last release, so it's ready after lunch, and I won't tag or deploy anything myself without your go-ahead.
Action: Find the latest release tag, list commits and pending changesets since it, and draft the changelog.

I'll fix the swallowed catch in the pdf render job so errors are logged with context and reported to the exception tracker, and rethrown or marked failed so the job doesn't die silently. I don't know which exception tracker we use from here, so I'll check the existing code for how errors are reported elsewhere and follow it. Then I'll commit it.
Action: Read the pdf render job, find the existing error reporting pattern, make the change with a test, run the tests, and commit.

I'll install dependencies in ~/code/acme-platform so the seed can run. I'll check the repo's required Node version (the .nvmrc and engines field) and the package manager first, since a mismatched Node version causes install errors. You'll also need a .env set up for the seed to run against a database, and I don't know where your secrets are kept for that machine, so I'll point you to the setup docs rather than guess.
Action: Check .nvmrc and package.json engines, run the install in ~/code/acme-platform, and report any errors.

I'll rename getSessionClaims to readSessionClaims everywhere: the definition, its callers, tests and the auth plugin. I'll grep for all references first, including docs, then run the api tests and typecheck to confirm nothing still imports the old name. The rename is separate from the clock skew change, so I'd keep it as its own commit.
Action: Grep for getSessionClaims across the repo, rename it, and run the typecheck and the api tests.

I'll do both pages in apps/web, which is Next.js App Router. /pricing is public, so it goes under the (marketing) route group with the plans table content in a ts file, and it must be added to the publicRoutes matcher in middleware.ts, otherwise Clerk will protect it. /settings/team goes under (dashboard) since it needs a signed-in user and lists org members. I see /pricing may already exist with placeholder prices that marketing hasn't confirmed, so I'll check what's there before building and not invent prices. I'll use theme tokens and not hard-coded colors.
Action: Check apps/web/app for existing pricing and settings routes, then build the missing pages and update middleware.ts.

Since the API is on Fastify 5, I'll write the x-org-id guard as a Fastify plugin in apps/api/src/plugins/, using a hook with the (request, reply) signature, and register it on the clients, invoices, orgs and uploads prefixes but not health or webhooks. It returns a 403 problem+json when the header is missing or doesn't match one of the session's orgs. I'll test it with app.inject().
Action: Look at the existing plugins in apps/api/src/plugins/ for conventions, write the guard and its tests, and run the api test suite.
